journal_text: I came to Claywater Station on the Blackwood Road. Travellers there pay Livia Varinius, the well-keeper, 2 drakes for the stop this season. Signs-For-The-Cargo, the landing's poler, now wants 1 drake from every walker who wades the ford. I'm to hear each keeper's side. Claywater Station is about 640 yards west of the signpost at Cartwright's Cross on the Blackwood Road, where the arms point to Gideon and to Leyawiin. Going west, a painted pole barrier stands in a field about 110 yards off the road on the right; that is the Drowning Gate. The station house roof shows about 100 yards on, ahead on the left. Livia Varinius keeps the well at the station house door, inside the low stone walls. Signs-For-The-Cargo poles the plank raft at the landing stage across the ford in the morning, about 65 yards north of the well. The round mud huts stand behind it on the far bank. If the road runs on into open marsh with no roofs in sight, I have passed it.
directions: From the Blackwood Road: Claywater Station is about 640 yards west of the signpost at Cartwright's Cross, where the arms point to Gideon and to Leyawiin. Going west, a painted pole barrier stands in a field about 110 yards off the road on the right; that is the Drowning Gate, and the station house roof shows about 100 yards on, ahead on the left. The well stands at the station house door, inside the low stone walls. From the well, the raft and the landing stage are about 65 yards to the north, across the ford, with the round mud huts behind them on the far bank. If the road runs on into open marsh with no roofs in sight, you have passed it.

journal_text: At Claywater Station, Livia Varinius told me she raised the station's charge to 2 drakes to pay a mason to re-line the cracked well in stone. Signs-For-The-Cargo told me the landing began charging walkers at the ford. The landing worked this ford before the well was dug. The landing will not haul stone for the station. Signs-For-The-Cargo says a crocodile has taken the landing's clay cut below the ford. The landing will hear terms only from whoever wins back the cut before the rains. I'm to kill the crocodile and bring back the clay basket that lies at the cut. The cut is below the ford on the station bank. From the well, I go about 45 yards west, outside the low stone walls, to where the river swings west under a bare clay bank and the water lies deep and dark. If the bank flattens into reeds, I have gone past it. Signs-For-The-Cargo says Takes-The-Short-Weight can tell what ails the station's water. She lives in the round mud hut on the landing bank, about 30 yards north of the raft. In the morning she sits at the landing's fire, about 50 yards north of the raft.
directions: The clay cut is below the ford on the station bank: from the well, go about 45 yards west, outside the low stone walls, to where the river swings west under a bare clay bank and the water lies deep and dark. If the bank flattens into reeds, you have gone past it. Takes-The-Short-Weight lives in the round mud hut on the landing bank, about 30 yards north of the raft; in the morning she sits at the landing's fire, about 50 yards north of the raft.

journal_text: I killed the crocodile at the clay cut below the ford at Claywater Station and have the landing's clay basket. I'm to put terms to Livia Varinius and to Signs-For-The-Cargo before the rains: one charge of 2 drakes a stop, 1 to each bank, with the landing's clay rammed in behind the cracked lining. Livia Varinius says a mason's lining will mend the well and mud has no place in it. She says the landing would take half a charge for water it never draws. I'm to find out whether the well has cracked before. Takes-The-Short-Weight can taste the station's water if I bring it to her in Livia Varinius's dipper. Signs-For-The-Cargo says the station only wants stone. He will not haul it. Livia Varinius is at the well in the morning, at the counter by the station house door in the afternoon and at the stable at dusk. Signs-For-The-Cargo poles the raft in the morning and is at the drying racks behind it in the afternoon.
directions: Livia Varinius is at the well in the morning, at the counter by the station house door in the afternoon and at the stable at dusk; Signs-For-The-Cargo poles the raft in the morning and is at the drying racks behind it in the afternoon.

journal_text: I brought Livia Varinius and Signs-For-The-Cargo to terms at Claywater Station: one charge of 2 drakes a stop, 1 to each bank. The landing has rammed its clay in behind the cracked lining before the rains. I killed the crocodile at the clay cut and gave the landing back its basket. Livia Varinius will send for no mason. Travellers no longer have a reason to wade below the cut at night. The ferry at the Drowning Gate is free to me from now on.

I found that travellers at Claywater Station paid Livia Varinius at the well and again at the ford. I paid Signs-For-The-Cargo 100 drakes to take no charge from walkers this season, so they pay once, at the well. The well is still cracked.

I found that travellers at Claywater Station paid Livia Varinius at the well and again at the ford. I also found that the well's lining has cracked and been mended every year. To keep that quiet, Livia Varinius has dropped her charge back to the old drake. Signs-For-The-Cargo has dropped the walkers' charge in answer. Livia Varinius will send for no mason. The well is still cracked. The ferry at the Drowning Gate is free to me from now on.
The rains came to Claywater Station before I made terms between Livia Varinius and Signs-For-The-Cargo. The well is still cracked. Travellers still pay at both banks or wade below the ford at night.

Livia Varinius is dead. The well at Claywater Station has no keeper now. The station's charge ended with her. Signs-For-The-Cargo keeps the landing's charge on the ford. The two charges cannot be settled now.
Signs-For-The-Cargo is dead. The raft at Claywater Station has no poler. The landing will make no terms with Livia Varinius and the station while it mourns. Both charges stand.
Mee-Sei, who cooks at the fire stand in Greenspring, told me that guests at the lodge have been falling sick, and that people blame his food. I'm to find out what is making them ill.
directions: The pool lies under the Hist, a few steps from the fire stand; the lodge, where the sick guests lie, faces it across the spring.

journal_text: The guests at the Greenspring lodge sicken from the spring, not from Mee-Sei's food. Only Im-Moro, the spring-keeper, may go into the pool under the Hist. I'm to get into the pool, with her leave or without it at night.
directions: The stone lip is on the lodge side of the pool; the Hist's roots go down into the water on the far side.

journal_text: I have gone into the pool under the Hist at Greenspring. I'm to search the spring's throat between the roots, where the water comes up.

A dead man lies staked in the throat of the spring at Greenspring, his wrists tied with rope, the stake left blank. That is what sickens the guests. I'm to find out who he was and who killed him, before the killer leaves.
directions: The lodge store is the locked room behind Haj-Tei's door; Reeh-Shaal sleeps in the lodge and goes to the stone lip after the lamps are out.

journal_text: The courier who vanished from the Greenspring lodge twelve days ago lies in the spring, and what I have found points to Reeh-Shaal, the guest who says she waits for a boat to Helstrom. I'm to confront her with what I hold, and I need two things to make it stand.

I named Reeh-Shaal before the people of Greenspring as the one who killed the Helstrom courier and staked him in the spring. Im-Moro has had the body raised and given to the Hist, and the root-herald holds Reeh-Shaal for Helstrom.
Reeh-Shaal is dead by my hand at Greenspring. Im-Moro has had the courier's body raised from the spring, and the guests should mend.
I took the sealed packet from Reeh-Shaal at Greenspring and let her go. Nobody there will learn who killed the courier.
I accused Tsono-Ra of the courier's murder at Greenspring, and I was wrong. The village has closed ranks against me, and Reeh-Shaal has taken the boat.
Reeh-Shaal has left Greenspring on the Helstrom boat. Whoever killed the courier in the spring has gone, and the guests are still sick.

I woke on the docks of Lilmoth among an Owing gang, with no memory of how I came to owe. Ux-Xeek is reading the work roll by the roll-house at the landward end of the docks. I'm to answer when she reaches my line.
directions: The roll-house stands at the landward end of the docks, where the planks meet Lilmoth's first street.

journal_text: Ux-Xeek found no name on my line of the Lilmoth work roll. Wuleen-Sei, the overseer, has given me Sal-Sei's feed jars. I'm to carry them east along the water to the hatching shed in Pusbottom, where the great root comes out of the bank below the Hist, and come back to the docks. Our own things are in a locked chest behind the roll-house.
directions: Pusbottom is the lane east of Lilmoth's square, below the Hist; the shed sits where the great root comes out of the bank. The docks are back west along the same lane.

journal_text: I carried Sal-Sei's jars to the shed in Pusbottom. When I came back to the docks of Lilmoth, a boat came in off the harbour. A tall Argonian woman with a knotted cord at her wrist killed the courier Mee-Tuja, took his satchel and set the roll-house burning. She looked at me and left. I'm to get off the burning docks by the lane east along the water toward Pusbottom.
directions: The fire is between me and the street; the lane to Pusbottom runs east along the water.

journal_text: The woman from the boat has gone from the Lilmoth docks, but her people are in the Pusbottom lane. I can hear cutting at the hatching shed, where Sal-Sei is, and Deesh-Duun is shouting from under the burning planks behind me. I'm to reach one of them; I cannot reach both.
directions: The shed is at the end of the lane where the root leaves the bank; the planks are back west behind the smoke.

journal_text: I ran for the hatching shed in Pusbottom. Two of the woman's people have cut the root that feeds the shed and are filling jars with its sap; Sal-Sei is on the ground. Behind me the planks have fallen in where Deesh-Duun was. I'm to drive the cutters off, then climb the lane east to the Hist's grove, away from the fire.
directions: From the shed the lane climbs east and up to the Hist's grove; Hereguard lies beyond the docks to the west.

journal_text: I went back for Deesh-Duun under the burning planks of the Lilmoth docks and pulled her out through the water. She saw the woman from the boat as close as I did. From the water I saw the cutters leave the hatching shed in Pusbottom with jars of sap, and Sal-Sei did not come out. Deesh-Duun will make her own way to Hereguard. I'm to get out of the smoke by the lane east up to the Hist's grove.
directions: The way out of the smoke climbs east up the lane to the Hist's grove, where the fire has not reached.

journal_text: Sal-Sei and Deesh-Duun are both dead on the Lilmoth docks. I'm to get out of the smoke by the lane up to the Hist's grove.
directions: The lane climbs east from Pusbottom to the grove.

journal_text: In the grove above Pusbottom I watched Lilmoth's Hist close. Its two tenders knelt, the light in its shrine went out and the sap stopped at the bowl. I'm to get out of Lilmoth to the west, to Hereguard Plantation, a swim across the harbour shallows from the docks or a walk round the shore past the rice paddies.
directions: Hereguard Plantation is one square west of the docks: a long swim across the harbour shallows, or the shore path past the rice paddies; its manor stands above the water.

journal_text: I reached Hereguard Plantation, west of Lilmoth, ahead of the fire. The survivors of the work detail are gathering below the manor. I'm to wait out the night with them and speak to whoever I saved after dawn.
directions: The survivors sit on the steps below Hereguard's manor, above the landing.

journal_text: I got out of Lilmoth with the clutch-keeper Sal-Sei. Before dawn he went back to the hatching shed in Pusbottom and came back grey: the eggs under the cut root are dead. Lilmoth's Hist has closed, and the work roll burned with the roll-house; nobody can say what I owe.

I got out of Lilmoth with Deesh-Duun, who saw the woman from the boat as close as I did. Word came at dawn that the clutch under the cut root in Pusbottom is dead, and Sal-Sei with it. Lilmoth's Hist has closed, and the work roll burned; nobody can say what I owe.
I got out of Lilmoth alone. Sal-Sei and Deesh-Duun are dead, and at dawn the gang said the clutch in Pusbottom is dead. Lilmoth's Hist has closed, and the work roll burned; nobody can say what I owe.

At Hereguard Plantation, west of Lilmoth, a Veiled Reed officer named Nesh-Deeka came off a boat in the night and is asking the survivors of the Lilmoth work detail what they saw. I'm to find her on the manor's porch and tell her what I know.
directions: Nesh-Deeka stands on the porch of the manor above Hereguard's landing.

journal_text: Nesh-Deeka of the Veiled Reed says the courier's satchel was Reed business. She wants me to go back to the burnt docks of Lilmoth, one square east of Hereguard, past the dock wardens, and read what the attackers left. I'm to look at the courier Mee-Tuja's body and his strap, and at the cut root by the hatching shed in Pusbottom. She gave me a Reed token to show the wardens.
directions: The docks are a swim east across the shallows, or the shore path past the paddies. The strap went through the planks by the body; Pusbottom is the lane east along the water.

journal_text: On the Lilmoth docks the courier's strap was cut low and clean, a soldier's stroke, and in Pusbottom the cut root was sealed with a black gum. The dock wardens say the overseer Wuleen-Sei ran into a fisher's cabin by Pusbottom. I'm to find her there, north of Pusbottom up the bank toward the town, and learn why the gang was kept at the dock end at noon.
directions: The cabin stands north of Pusbottom, up the bank toward the town, its door facing the water.

journal_text: Wuleen-Sei is dead in the fisher's cabin by Pusbottom, north of Pusbottom up the bank toward the town, and cannot say who paid her. Her strongbox is still there. I'm to open it and read her ledger.
directions: The cabin stands north of Pusbottom, up the bank toward the town, its door facing the water.

journal_text: Wuleen-Sei took a stranger's purse to keep the gang at the dock end of the Lilmoth docks, and the courier's strap was cut with a soldier's stroke. I'm to take the strap, the gum and what I learned of the overseer back to Nesh-Deeka on Hereguard's porch, and say whether Wuleen-Sei is to be named.
directions: Back west to Hereguard; Nesh-Deeka keeps to the manor's porch.

journal_text: Nesh-Deeka believes the attack was led by someone the Veiled Reed trained. She holds the Lilmoth roll's only copy, with my line blank, so the law counts me among the dead. She will keep it blank, and keep me unconnected, if I work for her quietly. I'm to give her my answer on Hereguard's porch, and I may ask a price.
I have taken the Veiled Reed's pardon from Nesh-Deeka at Hereguard Plantation. She will send word in the morning. I'm to sleep in the lean-to by the landing.
directions: The lean-to stands by the landing, below the manor.

journal_text: I am dreaming. I stand in fog among a ring of trees, and at the far side there is a gap like a door that nobody has built. A voice is speaking. I'm to walk to the door.
directions: The door is at the far end of the ring, straight ahead through the fog.

journal_text: Nesh-Deeka of the Veiled Reed is dead at Hereguard Plantation. The boat captain at the landing has brought me a letter from another Reed officer, Never-Writes-Twice, with the same offer and the roll's copy. I'm to read it.
directions: The boat captain stands at Hereguard's landing, below the manor.

journal_text: Never-Writes-Twice's letter offers the Veiled Reed's pardon on Nesh-Deeka's terms; the roll's copy stays blank and the law counts me dead, if I serve. I have kept the letter. I'm to sleep in the lean-to by the landing.
directions: The lean-to stands by the landing, below the manor.

journal_text: I woke at Hereguard Plantation. The Veiled Reed has pardoned me: on its copy of the Lilmoth roll my line stays blank, and the law counts me dead. The gang's months stand. Word came from the Reed that a village east along the coast, past Lilmoth, has a Hist that has closed like Lilmoth's.

I woke at Hereguard Plantation. The Veiled Reed struck the gang's months off its copy of the Lilmoth roll at my asking; in return my pardon holds only while I serve. Word came from the Reed that a village east along the coast, past Lilmoth, has a Hist that has closed like Lilmoth's.

The Veiled Reed sent me from Hereguard Plantation east along the coast past Lilmoth to the village of the Hatching Pools, a long day's walk, where the hatchery Hist has closed as Lilmoth's did. Its stilts stand over the pools with the tree above. I'm to find the warden-mother, Nurwul-Neel, and learn what happened.
directions: From Hereguard follow the coast east past Lilmoth, a landing with a boat captain, and the stilt houses of Alten Meirhall; keep the sea on the right. The village stands on stilts over its pools, the Hist above it.

journal_text: Nurwul-Neel, the warden-mother of the Hatching Pools, the stilt village east along the coast past Lilmoth, is dead. The village's chief says the tenders blame leeches, and the old tender Mee-Vei. I'm to see the pools and the root for myself.
directions: The village stands on stilts over its pools east along the coast past Lilmoth, Dock2's landing and Alten Meirhall; the Hist stands above it.

journal_text: At the Hatching Pools, the tenders say leeches have sickened the pools since the Hist closed, and that the old tender Mee-Vei cut the root. I'm to go down to the pools under the stilts and up to the cut root on the inland side, and see for myself.
directions: The pools lie under the village's stilts; the cut root comes down from the Hist on the inland side.

journal_text: The leeches in the Hatching Pools are fat on spilled sap; they came after the tree closed. Under the leech bed the cut root is sealed with the same black gum as Lilmoth's. The tenders say Mee-Vei goes to the root at night. I'm to watch the root from the reeds after dark, or ask him.
directions: The reeds on the inland side look onto the root; Mee-Vei comes after dark.

journal_text: Mee-Vei is dead, and cannot say what he saw at the root of the Hatching Pools. The black gum on the root runs off into the reeds to the south. I'm to follow it.
directions: The gum drips run south from the root through the reeds, two squares to a reed bed.

journal_text: Mee-Vei of the Hatching Pools is dead, and I found a cracked jar of the cutters' at a reed bed south of the village. I'm to follow their way east along the shallows below Longmont's walls, to wherever they went.
directions: East along the shallows below Longmont's walls to a sunk skiff; then north-east two squares to a dry rise among the alligator pools, where smoke shows by day.

journal_text: Mee-Vei washes the cut root of the Hatching Pools every night; he did not cut it. He saw three people leave by the reeds to the south. I'm to follow the gum drips south from the village, past a reed bed, then east below Longmont's walls, to wherever the cutters went.
directions: South two squares to a reed bed with a cracked jar; east along the shallows below Longmont's walls to a sunk skiff; then north-east two squares to a dry rise among the alligator pools, where smoke shows by day.

journal_text: The Unbound Root cut the Hist of the Hatching Pools and drew its sap into jars, which I have taken from their camp in the swamps. Nurwul-Neel has called the village to the Hist to judge Mee-Vei, living or dead. I'm to go back up to the tree and decide what I put before them.
directions: Back north-west along the trail to the village and up to the Hist.

journal_text: At the Hatching Pools I showed the village the leech, the black gum and the stolen sap, and Nurwul-Neel cleared Mee-Vei. The jars were emptied at the root, and the nest showed a little warmth. The Unbound Root has done this twice now. I'm to take the cutters' note to the Veiled Reed.

An An-Xileel officer has taken the Hist of the Hatching Pools under guard on my word. The tenders will not speak to me, but no one else will cut the root. I'm to take the cutters' note to the Veiled Reed.
I let Nurwul-Neel name Mee-Vei before the Hist of the Hatching Pools. He was sent from the village, the nest stays cold, and I kept the jars of sap. I'm to take the cutters' note to the Veiled Reed.

At the Hatching Pools I showed the village the leech, the black gum and the stolen sap, and Nurwul-Neel cleared Mee-Vei's name, too late for him. The jars were emptied at the root, and the nest showed a little warmth. I'm to take the cutters' note to the Veiled Reed.
Nurwul-Neel is dead, and the village's chief has sent to the An-Xileel to guard the Hist of the Hatching Pools. The tenders will not speak to me. I'm to take the cutters' note to the Veiled Reed.

After the Hatching Pools, the Veiled Reed's word reached me. I'm to take the ship from Lilmoth's eastern landing, past Pusbottom, across to the landing the boatmen call the fifth dock, then go north to Helstrom with the Reed's escort and report to the Veiled Reed's officer there, Never-Writes-Twice.
directions: The ship lies at the landing on the east side of Lilmoth harbour, past Pusbottom.

journal_text: Three raiders were waiting on the shore when the ship came in to the fifth dock, as if they knew I was coming. I'm to drive them off before the escort will land.

The shore at the fifth dock is clear; the raiders' leader carried a copy of the Reed's message. The two Reed escorts will walk me north through the marsh to Helstrom. I'm to keep them alive and stay on the raised path, about eight squares north, until the city's roofs show above the reeds.
directions: North from the fifth dock along the raised path for about eight squares; Helstrom's roofs show above the reeds. The doors in the hillside by the landing are locked.

journal_text: I reached Helstrom where the raised path ends among its houses. The low door on the west side as the path comes in from the south opens on a hall with an empty throne, the Scalded Throne, which a keeper still sweeps. I'm to find Never-Writes-Twice of the Veiled Reed behind the house door at the north end of the square, facing the path, and give her my report and the raiders' copy.
directions: The hall is the low door on the west side where the path comes in from the south; the Reed's rooms are behind the house door at the north end of the square, facing the path.

journal_text: Never-Writes-Twice of the Veiled Reed is dead in Helstrom. Her rooms are behind the house door at the north end of the square, facing the path, and her last orders should be on her desk. I'm to find them.

Never-Writes-Twice filed my report on the closed trees at once, and the raiders' copy tells her someone in her Helstrom office sold the Reed's message. She wants Reed watchers at the wounded trees, and the Tree-Minders must allow it. I'm to win Kaska-Meen's leave, in the grove at the north-east end of the square, past the last house door; Ei-Tuja, behind the house door on the west side of the square, north of the hall, may help for a price.
directions: The Tree-Minders keep the grove at the north-east end of the square, past the last house door, round the young Hist planted there; the debating house is behind the house door on the west side of the square, north of the hall, with a reed screen hung across it.

journal_text: Never-Writes-Twice's last orders, on her desk in Helstrom, ask for what she wanted, Reed watchers at the wounded trees, by the Tree-Minders' leave. I'm to win Kaska-Meen's leave, in the grove at the north-east end of the square, past the last house door; Ei-Tuja, behind the house door on the west side of the square, north of the hall, may help for a price.
directions: The Tree-Minders keep the grove at the north-east end of the square, past the last house door, round the young Hist planted there; the debating house is behind the house door on the west side of the square, north of the hall, with a reed screen hung across it.

journal_text: Kaska-Meen is dead, and the Tree-Minders of Helstrom will not speak to me or to the Veiled Reed. The watchers will not be posted.
I showed Kaska-Meen the black gum from the Hatching Pools, and she gave the Veiled Reed leave to watch the wounded trees. The Reed's office in Helstrom is open to me; Kaska-Meen is not.
I told Kaska-Meen the Tree-Minders were right to keep the trees to themselves. She will take me to the city's trees herself; the Veiled Reed's file says that I failed.

I paid Ei-Tuja to preach that a closed tree may be watched by any who mean it well, and Kaska-Meen yielded without yielding. The Veiled Reed will post its watchers, and Ei-Tuja reminds me what I owe him.

Root-Herald Ixo-Vaal of Greenspring asked me, for the Many-Root Conclave, to find out why the village's Hist is sickening. The village blames the salt works upstream. I'm to test the water before I believe them.
directions: The fork lies a short walk upstream of the river landing; the herald's house, with the salt sack at its door, faces the Hist.

journal_text: The salt in Greenspring's spring is not coming down the river. The couriers say the Hist's roots run into the flooded galleries of the Drowned Stair. I'm to go down and take water at each landing.
directions: From Greenspring take the road to the Gate-Side Camp outside Helstrom's gate; the guides there show the stair's mouth, where the deep water starts.

journal_text: The water in the Drowned Stair grows saltier the deeper I go. I'm to reach the deepest chamber, beyond one breath, and see where the salt comes in.

Deep in the Drowned Stair, a channel has been cut by hand into a brine seam, and the floods push the brine into Greenspring's roots. The cut is old. I'm to learn who made it, and Vees-Wai, the tree-minder, reads the old stakes.

Greenspring's founders cut the channel to kill a rival grove downstream, and their deed is killing their own Hist. Ixo-Vaal has called the office-holders to the Hist. I'm to put what I found before them and argue for a cure, and for whether the founders are named.
The office-holders of Greenspring sealed the founders' cut and named the deed at the Hist. The tree should mend, and Greenspring now owes the people of the dead grove an answer.
The office-holders of Greenspring sealed the founders' cut and agreed to say nothing of who made it. The tree should mend.
Greenspring chose to reopen the founders' cut downstream. Their Hist is spared, and the dead grove's land will flood with brine again.
